why: Flaws in THIS package found by the uuidna session that released 0.1.5, deposited here because the write channels could not carry them: uuidna_evidence returned {} for a deposit (no content and no refusal, which a caller reads as success), and qpu storage answers 401 without QPU_WRITE_TOKEN, which is the owner's to set. Recorded in the repository instead, because nothing lives in a private note.

unsent_through.result: returned {} — an empty envelope: no content and no refusal
401 — QPU_WRITE_TOKEN is not set in that environment and is the owner's to set

flaws.measured: The v0.1.5 publish run FAILED for e3cc72dffa01ddcd53f535e96229a5180435fc82, while npm itself succeeded: the registry serves 0.1.5 as latest, dist.attestations carries SLSA provenance, and gitHead equals the v0.1.5 tag commit. verify-release reports 4 of 5 green and names the fifth — Zenodo still holds v0.1.4 after 30 rounds.
flaws.reading: The failure is DOWNSTREAM of publishing. publish.yml's own comment says it does three things and confirms none of them; verify-release is the arm that confirms, so a failed run beside a live package means the release is LIVE and INCOMPLETE. A run status alone cannot tell those two apart, which is the thing worth fixing: the run should say which of the five checks it failed.
flaws.owes: Distinguish a webhook that fired late from one that never fired — ask Zenodo by concept DOI after the run, not inside it.

flaws.measured: package.json ci = lean && test && proof && mutate && test:scripts. No workflow invokes it; ci.yml re-lists the steps by hand. Before this session ci.yml named ONE scripts test (outage:test), so the leads, pace, percall and temporal suites ran in no chain at all — four of five guard suites unreachable while the board was green. All five pass; they were never asked.
flaws.reading: A list somebody edits is a list somebody forgets. The discovery half is cured — ci.yml now runs test:scripts, which globs scripts/*.test.mjs, so a suite added tomorrow runs the day it exists.
flaws.owes: The duplication between `npm run ci` and ci.yml is two hand lists that must agree and nothing checks that they do.

flaws.measured: In a clean install of the published 0.1.5 tarball with no network, 14 of 101 *Holds predicates do not hold. qpuApisLiveHolds, qpuCitationsLiveHolds, qpuComposeHolds, qpuComposeLiveHolds and qpuCrossHolds throw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading holds)'; qpuCiteHolds returns false.
flaws.reading: A consumer importing the package offline receives a TypeError from an internal rather than a refusal naming the missing instrument. qpu's own kernelPresent() carries the right law: an absent instrument VOIDS the judgement and says so by name, because a trial whose instrument is missing carries no information about the subject.
flaws.owes: NOT VERIFIED against a live-host run — the in-context suite passes 173/173, so this is reported as a shape, not a verdict.

flaws.measured: uuidna's kernel-probe writes lean/_wave_probe.<pid>.lean, and its suite runs --test-isolation=none, so every test shares one pid: two probe() calls resolve to one path and each unlinks under the other. Seen as ENOENT inside a landing's clean worktree while passing standalone.
flaws.reading: This is uuidna's defect, reported here because qpu carries the same probe pattern and the same 'one probe file per process' comment. A green that holds only while nothing else probes is not a green.
flaws.owes: Cured in uuidna with a per-call counter — deterministic, no clock and no random. qpu should check whether its own probe paths are per-call rather than per-process.

given_to_qpu_this_session: scripts/walls.mjs — the bare-wall finder ported from uuidna with both corrections uuidna paid for: an unreadable file is named UNMEASURED and never folded into clean, and the keyword list admits the very cure the finding prints. 23 walls measured, 9 controls including both failure directions.
ci.yml discovers scripts/*.test.mjs by glob instead of naming one file.
honest: Every claim here is a measurement taken in that session against this package or its published tarball, not a reading of qpu source. Where something was not verified, the row says so.
